no_rule_findings.finding: Massachusetts state law (M.G.L. c. 40P, § 4) bars cities and towns from enacting, maintaining or enforcing rent control of any kind. The only exception is narrow: it allows voluntary rent control with compensation to owners, cannot apply to owners of fewer than 10 units or to units with fair market rent over $400, and cannot regulate evictions. The document states no statewide rent cap.
